# Plan: deterministic skill-list ordering (CEO review — Step 0 checkpoint)

## Context

Users compare skill listings in scripts and reviews, so a listing whose order
depends on directory enumeration order is noise in diffs and flaky in tests.
The draft under review (PLAN.md) makes the existing listing path sort registered
skill names deterministically before rendering, while keeping skill membership,
aliases, metadata and text/JSON output formats unchanged, with tests for
mixed-case names and differing directory enumeration order.

This file is a checkpoint, not the review report. The user asked for the
review-mode decision only; the substantive review (Sections 1–11, required
outputs, GSTACK REVIEW REPORT) runs in a later invocation.

## Pre-review system audit (2026-10-04)

Real problem: listing order varies with filesystem enumeration, so scripted
comparisons and reviews see spurious diffs. Target outcome: identical input
set always renders in identical order. Do-nothing cost: ongoing false diffs and
order-dependent test flakiness. The plan addresses the pain directly (sort at
the listing path), not a proxy.

### 0B. Existing code leverage
Pending: the listing codebase is not in this checkout. The substantive review
must locate the existing listing path and registry and confirm the sort is a
single insertion there (no new abstraction). Open question for that review:
sort key semantics (case-sensitive byte order vs. case-insensitive with a

The plan moves toward the ideal without over-reaching.

No new approach decision was needed. The plan names a single approach; the only
